name: LAPACKE
reason: C interface (wrapper) to Fortran LAPACK, so there is nothing to beat. The only performance statement in the LAPACKE README (github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/tree/master/LAPACKE) is that, because of possible extra transpositions and per-call workspace allocation, a routine called through this interface may need more memory and run slower than the corresponding LAPACK routine. No benchmark numbers anywhere reachable; the netlib page listed in the seed (netlib.org/lapack/lapacke.html) was not fetched.

name: libsequence
listed_description: A C++ library for representing and analyzing population genetics data.
reason: No numeric comparison against any other library. README has no benchmarks; there is no benchmark directory. REVISION_HISTORY.md and ChangeLog only record speedups against its own earlier versions (for example a 10-fold speed-up of PolySNP statistics and a 6-fold speed-up of operator>>), which are not a recognizable baseline. A 2005 Bioperl mailing-list remark that libsequence statistics would be roughly 'a bazillion' times faster than Bioperl is anecdotal with no numbers (WebSearch snippet only). Repo is GPL-3.0 and archived by its owner on 2023-10-12.

name: LibTomMath
reason: No claim of being faster than anything. The author's manual (doc/bn.tex in github.com/libtom/libtommath, section 'Purpose of LibTomMath') states the library was not written with bleeding-edge performance in mind, that it is slower than GnuMP and than GnuPG v1.2.3's math, and that on x86 the difference is normally a factor of two for modular exponentiation (v0.28-0.35 era numbers, no methodology). The README has no benchmarks. Third-party comparisons found (libzahl STATUS/commit log) compare libzahl with GMP and TomsFastMath, not LibTomMath as the winner; TomsFastMath is the fork that claims to be faster than LibTomMath.

name: LibTomPoly
reason: README (raw.githubusercontent.com/libtom/libtompoly/HEAD/README.md) and the repo page have no mention of speed, benchmarks or timing; it is a small polynomial-basis arithmetic layer on LibTomMath (9 commits on develop, 40 stars). No comparison against any named baseline found.

name: LiquidFun
reason: Directional claim only, no numbers. The v1.1.0 release notes say the release 'speeds-up the simulation' and add ARM NEON optimization (b2ParticleSystem::UpdateContacts rewritten with NEON, optional 16-bit particle indices), with no measured gain and no named baseline. LiquidFun is Box2D plus a particle/fluid system; the programmer's guide only says its solver is 'high performance' and 'order N'. WebSearch found no benchmark against Box2D, Bullet or ODE. Repo archived by owner on 2026-02-13, last commit 2018-01-10, no repo-level README to check.
